newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds edge up, focus on new issues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds edge up, focus on new issues.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond prices were up slightly tracking U.S. Treasuries in light trading, as players focused on the new issue arena, dealers said.
Spreads against U.S. Treasuries were mostly unchanged across most maturities, they added.
"It's relatively quiet in the secondary market," said one high-grade trader. "A lot of attention is being focused on new issues such as Nationsbank's and the Ford global deal."
Earlier, Ford Motor unit, Ford Motor Credit Corp priced $1.0 billion in five-year global bonds to yield 48 basis points over Treasuries via Goldman Sachs & Co.
"Yesterday tobacco debt tightened up but it's wider by a basis point today," one trader said.
Philip Morris 7.65 percent debt due 2008 were 96 basis points bid, 93 basis points offered, while RJR debt was seen trading at 245 basis points bid and 235 basis points offered.
Meanwhile, Service Corp International debt due 2006 widened out to trade at 80 bid, 65 offered. Dealers said the paper was trading at 63 basis points bid, before the news.
On Monday, Service Corp said it proposed acquiring Loewen Group Inc in a stock-for-stock exchange that values Loewen at $43 per share.
Loewen Corp debt tightened between 20 to 30 basis points since news of the proposal, traders said.
Loewen's 7.50 percent debt due 2001 was seen bid at 120 basis points, 90 basis points offered. Paper due 2003 was seen trading at 140 basis points bid, 110 offered, traders said.
"I think people are pretty unsure whether Ray Loewen's will take the deal," one trader said. "It's a pretty closely held company and people are not sure what they'll do."
Other traders cited uncertainty about whether Service Corp would be willing to pursue a hostile takeoveer if the $43 per share offer were rebuffed by Loewen.
Turning to the junk sector, prices were quoted unchanged to up 1/8 in light trading with new issues once again stealing the spotlight, traders said.
"The broader market is unchanged to up an 1/8," said one high-yield trader. "Activity is starting to pick up again as new issues hit the market."

Speedy Muffler King's new 10-year issue traded up at 101-5/8 bid on the break, after pricing at par. Euromax's recent debt issue was also quoted up at 101-3/8 bid, 101-1/2 offer, after pricing at par, traders said.
